title: 2024年12月 第1套

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Okay then.
lines.translation: 那好吧,我说吧

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: OK then, this here is your yearly performance review.
lines.translation: 好吧,这是你年度业绩审查

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You've been with the company for 3 years and under my direct supervision for the past 12 months.
lines.translation: 你已经在公司呆了三年了 在过去的12个月里 在我的直接监督下

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Your report is mostly good.
lines.translation: 你的报告大部分是好的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But there are a couple of issues we must discuss.
lines.translation: 但是,我们必须讨论几个问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The report is yours to take with you.
lines.translation: 你的报告随你带走

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: We'll go through the main points together now.
lines.translation: 我们现在一起通过要点

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And you can come through it in greater detail later.
lines.translation: 你可以稍后再详细分析

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Do you have any questions before we start?
lines.translation: 在我们开始之前 你有什么问题吗?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: No, sir.
lines.translation: 没有，先生。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I'll get straight to it then.
lines.translation: 那我就直说了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It is evident that you are a hard worker.
lines.translation: 很明显，你工作很努力。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You are punctual and industrious.
lines.translation: 你很守时，也很勤奋。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Furthermore, you have strong analytical skills and attention to detail.
lines.translation: 此外，你有很强的分析能力，而且注重细节。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The company, myself included, is happy with your productivity and overall performance.
lines.translation: 公司，包括我在内，都对你的工作效率和整体表现感到满意。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Thank you.
lines.translation: M：谢谢。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I appreciate the recognition.
lines.translation: 能得到这样的认可，我很感谢。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Do you agree, then, with this depiction so far?
lines.translation: 那么，到目前为止，你同意这份描述吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Yeah, it's a little simplistic perhaps.
lines.translation: 嗯，也许有点过于简单了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But that's to be expected from this kind of evaluation.
lines.translation: 不过，这种评估大概就是这样。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Sure.
lines.translation: 当然。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Would you want to add anything?
lines.translation: 你想补充些什么吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Your comments can be added to the report if you wish.
lines.translation: 如果你愿意，我们可以把你的意见加到报告里。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Oh, there's no need.
lines.translation: 哦，没必要。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's a flattering portrayal really.
lines.translation: 说真的，这份描述已经很恭维我了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Thank you, though.
lines.translation: 不过还是谢谢你。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: OK.
lines.translation: 好。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This leads me to the not-so-good part.
lines.translation: 这就说到不太好的部分了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This mostly centers around one behavioral aspect—your ability to work with others.
lines.translation: 主要涉及一个行为方面的问题，也就是你与他人合作的能力。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I see.
lines.translation: 我明白了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Yes.
lines.translation: 是的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: As you already know, over the last several months, there have been some complaints raised about your communication style.
lines.translation: 你也知道，过去几个月里，有人对你的沟通方式提出了一些投诉。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Of course, we already had like three meetings about this.
lines.translation: 当然了，我们已经为这件事开过大概三次会了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Look, all I'm going to say is that it was never my intention to offend anyone.
lines.translation: 听着，我只想说，我从来没打算冒犯任何人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Simply put, I don't like to write long emails, because, frankly, I think they're a waste of time.
lines.translation: 简单来说，我不喜欢写很长的邮件，因为坦白说，我觉得那是在浪费时间。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Conciseness is efficiency.
lines.translation: 简洁就是效率。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I feel that writing long emails hurts that same productivity you praised me for just a minute ago.
lines.translation: 我觉得写长邮件会损害你刚才还在称赞的那种工作效率。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And I already apologized if anyone was offended.
lines.translation: 如果有人觉得受到了冒犯，我也已经道过歉了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But to be perfectly honest, I think anyone who was offended was being a little too sensitive.
lines.translation: 但说句完全坦诚的话，我认为那些感到被冒犯的人有点太敏感了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 1-4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题1 -4是基于你刚才听到的谈话

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 1. What are the speakers most probably doing?
lines.translation: 第 1 题：说话者最有可能在做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 2. What does the woman say she appreciates?
lines.translation: 第 2 题：女士说她欣赏什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 3. What has given rise to some complaints about the woman?
lines.translation: 第 3 题：什么引发了一些关于女士的投诉?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 4. Why doesn't the woman like to write long emails?
lines.translation: 第 4 题：女士为什么不喜欢写长邮件?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Conversation 2.
lines.translation: 对话2。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So tell me, why do you wish to study medicine?
lines.translation: M：那么请告诉我，你为什么想学医？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I've always wanted to be a doctor.
lines.translation: W：我一直都想成为一名医生。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I come from a small town where healthcare was never the best.
lines.translation: 我来自一个医疗条件始终不太好的小镇。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And I think that had a profound effect on me.
lines.translation: 我觉得这对我产生了深远的影响。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: As a child, I remember thinking how great it would be to serve the community and cure people!
lines.translation: 小时候，我记得自己常常想，要是能服务社区、治愈病人，那该多好啊！

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What other people or events in your life have shaped your interest in becoming a doctor?
lines.translation: M：你生活中的其他哪些人或哪些事情促使你产生了成为医生的兴趣？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, that's hard to say.
lines.translation: W：这个很难说。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I would certainly say my parents have been a key factor.
lines.translation: 我当然会说，我的父母是一个关键因素。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They always pushed me to study hard.
lines.translation: 他们总是督促我努力学习。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And I certainly wouldn't be here without their support.
lines.translation: 要不是他们的支持，我肯定不会坐在这里。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I guess I was also immensely fortunate to have good teachers and friends around me.
lines.translation: 我想，我也非常幸运，身边有优秀的老师和朋友。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: At the end of the day, I've always been surrounded by a positive environment conducive to my working hard and pursuing my dreams.
lines.translation: 总的来说，我一直处在一个积极向上的环境中，这个环境促使我努力学习、追逐梦想。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Is there any medical branch that you would like to specialize in?
lines.translation: M：你有没有想专攻的医学分支？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I haven't decided yet.
lines.translation: W：我还没决定。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's still early days.
lines.translation: 现在还早。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: However, if I had to say, internal medicine.
lines.translation: 不过，如果一定要说的话，我想选内科。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Why internal medicine?
lines.translation: M：为什么是内科？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I know it's no picnic.
lines.translation: W：我知道这可不是件轻松的事。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But I find it the most intriguing, because it covers so much and ties together so many other specialties.
lines.translation: 但我觉得内科最有意思，因为它涉及的范围很广，还把许多其他专科联系在了一起。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Thank you.
lines.translation: M：谢谢。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Now I'd like to address your academic history and projected grades.
lines.translation: 现在我想谈谈你的学业经历和预期成绩。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: We like to think of ourselves as a prestigious institution with a highly competitive and promising student body.
lines.translation: 我们愿意把自己看作一所享有盛誉的院校，拥有一批竞争力强、前途光明的学生。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: As you know, to get into our programmes, you need at least 85% score in the entrance exam.
lines.translation: 你知道，要进入我们的课程，入学考试至少要考到85%。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Do you think you can attain this?
lines.translation: 你觉得自己能达到这个分数吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I think so.
lines.translation: W：我想可以。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Yes.
lines.translation: 是的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I'm looking at your school grades now and I'll be honest.
lines.translation: 我现在在看你的成绩 说实话

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's a bit of a mixed bag.
lines.translation: 有点混杂

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You do get top grades here and there, but you are not very… Shall we say "consistent"?
lines.translation: 你确实有优等成绩 但你不是很...

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I see no problem in making you a conditional offer, but consider yourself warned, our entrance exam is, to use your own words, no picnic.
lines.translation: 我看不出有什么问题 让你有条件的报价, 但考虑到你自己警告, 我们的入学考试, 用你自己的话来说, 不是野餐。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 5. What does the woman say she has always wanted to do since childhood?
lines.translation: 第 5 题：女士说她从童年起就一直想做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 6. What do we learn about the woman's parents from the conversation?
lines.translation: 第 6 题：从对话中我们对女士的父母了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 7. Why does the woman say she wants to choose internal medicine as her specialty?
lines.translation: 第 7 题：女士为什么说她想选择内科学作为专业?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 8. How does the man describe the woman's school grades?
lines.translation: 第 8 题：男士如何描述女士的学校成绩?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Section B, directions.
lines.translation: B节,方向。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In this section you will hear two passages.
lines.translation: 在本节中,你们将听到两段。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: At the end of each passage you will hear three or four questions.
lines.translation: 在每一段的结尾 你会听到三个或四个问题

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
lines.translation: 发言的通过和提问将只讲一次。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices, marked A, B, C and D.
lines.translation: 听到一个问题,你必须从四个选择中选择最好的答案, 标记为A、B、C和D。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
lines.translation: 在答题单单行的答题表一中标出相应的字母。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Passage 1.
lines.translation: 通行证1号。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Logging into your email account can sometimes feel like trying to hack into the Pentagon.
lines.translation: 登录电子邮箱账户有时感觉就像试图入侵五角大楼。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If you follow all of the guidelines, you need to use a different password for every one of your accounts; use an incomprehensible variety of letters, numbers, and symbols; sign up for two-step verification; and change every password every time one of them is compromised.
lines.translation: 如果遵循所有指南，你需要为每个账户使用不同的密码；使用由字母、数字和符号组成的令人难以理解的组合；注册两步验证；并且每当其中一个密码遭到泄露时，就更改所有密码。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: More often than not, you then have to choose photos that include a street sign, as this apparently provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being.
lines.translation: 更常见的是，接下来你还必须选择包含街道标志的照片，因为这显然能向电脑提供确凿证据，证明你确实是人类。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's no small wonder most of us forget our passwords more often than our keys.
lines.translation: 难怪我们大多数人忘记密码的次数比忘记钥匙的次数还多。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Now a new peer-reviewed study by researchers at Aalto University in Finland is attempting to figure out why we forget our passwords in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon.
lines.translation: 如今，芬兰阿尔托大学的研究人员开展了一项新的同行评议研究，试图弄清我们为何会忘记密码，以帮助终结这一令人沮丧的现象。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Their findings suggest that how likely you are to remember your password has less to do with the password itself and more to do with how often you anticipate using it.
lines.translation: 他们的研究结果表明，你记住密码的可能性有多大，与密码本身的关系较小，而更多地取决于你预期使用它的频率。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Which is to say: you are far more likely to remember a complicated password if you know you'll frequently be using it to log into an account than you are to remember a simple password for an account that you don't expect to log into very often.
lines.translation: 也就是说，如果你知道自己会经常使用一个复杂密码登录某个账户，那么你记住它的可能性要远高于记住一个简单密码的可能性，后者所对应的账户是你预计不会经常登录的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The researchers advise websites to include more of an incentive for users to log in more often in order to help them remember their secret codes.
lines.translation: 研究人员建议网站为用户更频繁登录提供更多激励，以帮助他们记住自己的密码。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 9. Why do we often have to choose photos that include a street sign to log into our email accounts?
lines.translation: 第 9 题：为什么我们在登录电子邮件账户时经常需要选择包含街道标志的照片?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 10. What do researchers at a university in Finland aim to do in their new study?
lines.translation: 第 10 题：芬兰一所大学的研究人员在他们的新研究中旨在做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 11. What do the researchers advise websites to do at the end of the passage?
lines.translation: 第 11 题：研究人员在文章末尾建议网站做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 4 years ago, Jenny Wainer was in a fitness slump.
lines.translation: 四年前,珍妮·维纳 在一个健身房的贫民窟。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Four years ago, Jenny Weiner was in a fitness slump.
lines.translation: 四年前 珍妮·魏纳在健身房倒塌

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: She wanted to improve her physical and mental health.
lines.translation: 她希望改善自己的身心健康。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: However, her workouts lacked intensity without a proper training programme to follow.
lines.translation: 然而,由于没有适当的培训方案,她的锻炼缺乏强度。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: When she went to the gym, her daily ritual predominantly involved easy exercise options like jogging; she avoided more formidable exercises like lifting weights.
lines.translation: 当她去健身房时,她的日常仪式主要包括慢跑等轻松的锻炼选择;她避免了举重等更艰巨的锻炼。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: A personal trainer who might push her was out of the question.
lines.translation: 一位可能推她的个人教练 已经不可能了

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The extravagant cost was just unaffordable.
lines.translation: 奢侈的代价实在太低了

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: She then discovered the fitness phone app Slimmeretics.
lines.translation: 然后她发现了健身电话应用程序 消毒剂。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: To use the app, you first input your profile about your previous training experiences and preferences, as well as your desired goals.
lines.translation: 要使用此应用程序, 您首先要输入您先前的培训经验和偏好, 以及您想要达到的目标的简介 。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: A virtual coach then uses that information to suggest a personalised training regime.
lines.translation: 虚拟教练然后利用这些信息来建议个性化培训制度。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: After the workout, the app's artificial intelligence software system gives feedback from Ms. Weiner and its other 53 million users around the world to adjust future training sessions.
lines.translation: 软件的人工智能软件系统在开发后,从Weiner女士及其世界各地5 300万用户那里反馈反馈意见,以调整今后的培训课程。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Now Ms. Weiner finds the workouts exciting.
lines.translation: 现在魏纳小姐觉得健身很刺激

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This is because no two are ever the same.
lines.translation: 这是因为没有两个人永远一样。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: As a result, the app has helped her to lose more than 25 kilograms.
lines.translation: 因此,该应用程序帮助她损失了25公斤以上。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The app's mathematical approach can arrange a more meticulous workout schedule.
lines.translation: 应用软件的数学方法可以安排一个更加细致的工程计划。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This has led to optimal results.
lines.translation: 这已导致取得最佳结果。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: However, some experts think that apps cannot replace human personal trainers.
lines.translation: 然而,一些专家认为,应用软件不能取代人的个人培训员。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: An app cannot understand human behavior.
lines.translation: 应用程序无法理解人类的行为。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It will not comprehend that there are competing interests outside of health and fitness.
lines.translation: 它不会理解在健康和健康之外存在着相互竞争的利益。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Additionally, a human trainer can add compassion to the workout.
lines.translation: 此外,人类训练师可以给锻炼工作增添同情心。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: He can also make exercise fun and sustainable.
lines.translation: 他还可以使运动变得有趣和可持续。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Trainers can monitor whether a person is doing exercises correctly.
lines.translation: 教员可以监测一个人是否在正确练习。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This can safeguard against injuries.
lines.translation: 这可以防止伤害。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: An app cannot perceive such subtleties.
lines.translation: 应用程序无法感觉到这种微妙之处 。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 12. What was the problem Jenny Weiner encountered four years ago?
lines.translation: 第 12 题：四年前Jenny Weiner遇到了什么问题?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 13. What can the fitness phone app Slimmeretics do according to the passage?
lines.translation: 第 13 题：根据文章,健身手机应用程序Slimmeretics能做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 14. Why does the passage say Jenny Weiner now finds the workouts exciting?
lines.translation: 第 14 题：文章为什么说Jenny Weiner现在觉得锻炼令人兴奋?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 15. What do some experts think of fitness apps like Slimmeretics?
lines.translation: 第 15 题：一些专家如何看待像Slimmeretics这样的健身应用程序?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Section C, directions.
lines.translation: C节,方向。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In this section you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
lines.translation: 在本节中,你们将听取三场讲座或会谈录音,然后是三四个问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Recordings will be played only once.
lines.translation: 录音只播放一次。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D. Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
lines.translation: 在听到一个问题后,您必须选择四个选项中的最佳答案,四个选项标有A、B、C和D。然后在答题表1上用单行通过中心标出相应的字母。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Recording 1 All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules which include deferring to superiors and respecting the property of others Oxford University has concluded.
lines.translation: 1 所有社会都受到七项普遍道德规则的制约,包括服从上级和尊重牛津大学所缔结的其他人的财产。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules, which include deferring to superiors and respecting the property of others, Oxford University has concluded.
lines.translation: 牛津大学得出结论，所有社会都由七条普遍的道德规则维系在一起，其中包括服从上级和尊重他人财产。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Although many cultures are moving towards more liberal, less hierarchical organizations, the new research suggests that traditional power structures and basic values of charity and brotherhood are the cornerstones of successful societies.
lines.translation: 尽管许多文化正朝着更加自由、等级制度更弱的组织形式发展，但这项新研究表明，传统的权力结构以及慈善和兄弟情谊等基本价值观，才是成功社会的基石。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The huge study of 60 different cultures around the world found that all communities operate under seven basic moral codes.
lines.translation: 对世界各地60种不同文化的大规模研究发现,所有社区都遵循七项基本道德准则。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Those universal rules are: help your family, help your group, return favors, be brave, defer to superiors, divide resources fairly, and respect the property of others.
lines.translation: 这些普遍规则是: 帮助你的家庭, 帮助你的群体, 回报恩惠, 勇敢,服从上司, 公平分配资源, 尊重他人的财产。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The character traits held for every kind of community, be they traditional hunter gatherers or advanced civilizations, helping to uphold civilized society and foster social cooperation, researchers found.
lines.translation: 研究人员发现,各种社区,无论是传统的狩猎采集者还是先进的文明,都具有特征,有助于维护文明社会,促进社会合作。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: "Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code," said Dr. Oliver Scott Curry, lead author and senior researcher at Oxford.
lines.translation: 牛津大学首席作者兼高级研究员Oliver Scott Curry博士说,

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: "These seven moral rules appear to be universal across cultures, because people face the same social problems.
lines.translation: "这七项道德规则似乎跨越各种文化而具有普遍性, 因为人们面对同样的社会问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Even if some of these traits look right-wing or conservative, for example, deferring to authority, left-wing people will still have a group loyalty and deference to someone or something.
lines.translation: 即使其中一些特征看起来是右翼或保守的,例如服从权威,左翼人民仍将对某个人或某些东西有团体的忠诚和顺从。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This shows there really is more that unites us than divides us."
lines.translation: 这说明我们真正团结的 多于分裂的。”

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The study published in Current Anthropology is the largest and most comprehensive and widespread survey of morals ever conducted and aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality.
lines.translation: 这项发表于《当代人类学》的研究，是迄今开展的规模最大、最全面且覆盖范围最广的道德调查，旨在 выяс明不同社会是否拥有不同版本的道德观。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The team accessed the world's best archives to analyze accounts from more than 600 sources of 60 societies around the world.
lines.translation: 研究团队查阅了世界上最权威的档案资料，分析了来自世界各地60个社会的600多份资料记载。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They found that the seven rules were considered morally good in all societies and were observed across all continents, religions and politics.
lines.translation: 他们发现，在所有社会中，这七条规则都被视为合乎道德的准则，并且在各大洲、各种宗教和不同政治体系中都得到遵守。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: However, some communities valued certain rules more highly than others.
lines.translation: 不过，一些群体对某些规则的重视程度高于其他规则。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Dr. Curry hopes that this research helps to promote mutual understanding between people of different cultures and appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ.
lines.translation: Curry博士希望这项研究有助于促进不同文化人民之间的相互了解,增进对我们的共同点以及我们不同的方式和原因的认识。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Co-author professor Harvey Whitehouse said social scientists should now set about testing the theory in the field, rather than relying on old data.
lines.translation: 他说：“这项研究建立在对世界各地文化的历史描述之上。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: "This study was based on historical descriptions of cultures around the world," he said.
lines.translation: 这些描述是在独立于我们所检验的理论、且早于该理论提出的情况下形成的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: "These descriptions were made independent of and prior to the theory we're testing.
lines.translation: 今后，如果社会科学家认真对待道德理论的检验，就需要在实地以更加系统的方式收集新数据。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In future, if social scientists are serious about testing theories of morality, they will need to gather new data, more systematically, out in the field."

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 16. What do we learn from the conclusion of the Oxford University researchers?
lines.translation: 第 16 题：我们从牛津大学研究人员的结论中了解到什么？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 17. What did the new study by Oxford researchers aim to do?
lines.translation: 第 17 题：牛津研究人员的新研究旨在做什么？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 18. What does Harvey Whitehouse think social scientists should do to theories of morality?
lines.translation: 第 18 题：Harvey Whitehouse认为社会科学家应该如何对待道德理论？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Recording too.
lines.translation: 也录制

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: When it comes to food, color is money.
lines.translation: 说到食品，颜色就是金钱。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Food companies know that better color gives better prices, so they ensure that their products are attractive in color to bolster earnings.
lines.translation: 食品公司深知，颜色越好，价格就越高，因此它们会确保产品的色泽具有吸引力，以增加收益。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Oranges, for example, have to meet specific color standards.
lines.translation: 例如，橙子必须符合特定的色泽标准。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And oranges are just the beginning.
lines.translation: 而橙子还只是开始。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: There are color standards for foods including French fries, tomatoes, pumpkins, olives, honey and cherries.
lines.translation: 包括炸薯条、西红柿、南瓜、橄榄、蜂蜜和樱桃在内的食品，都有相应的色泽标准。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The attention to color is for good reason.
lines.translation: 人们之所以如此重视颜色，是有充分理由的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: For all the talk of the tongue, our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience.
lines.translation: 尽管人们总是在谈论舌头，但我们的眼睛实际上可能是饮食体验中最重要的部分。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision, while only a percent or two is given over to taste faculties, and the result is that color actually changes how we taste food.
lines.translation: 我们大脑的大量功能都用于处理视觉信息，而分配给味觉功能的只有百分之一或百分之二，其结果是，颜色确实会改变我们品尝食物时的感受。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Scientists have demonstrated many times the importance of color to taste.
lines.translation: 科学家已经多次展示了颜色对品味的重要性。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In a 1980s study, for example, test participants were asked to name the flavor of the beverage they were drinking without being able to see that beverage.
lines.translation: 例如,在1980年代的一项研究中,测试参与者被要求说明他们喝的饮料的口味,而没有看到饮料。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Only one in five was able to identify it as orange.
lines.translation: 五分之一的人能认出它为橙色

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But when they were allowed to see what they were drinking which was orange in color, each of them identified the orange flavor.
lines.translation: 但当他们被允许看他们喝什么时, 喝什么颜色是橙色的, 每人都认出了橙色的口味。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And when a drink that was lime flavor was colored orange, nearly half of respondents identified the flavor of the beverage as orange.
lines.translation: 当一杯是石灰味的饮料是彩色橙色时 将近一半的受访者认为饮料的味道是橙色

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: None made that mistake when the beverage was green in color.
lines.translation: 当饮料是绿色的颜色时,没有人犯错。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What's happening when someone fails to identify the flavor of a beverage they can't see or that has an abnormal color?
lines.translation: 当有人没认出他们看不见的饮料的味道 或者有异常颜色时会怎样?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Is it that participants can't discern what the flavor is, and so rely on visual cues?
lines.translation: 难道参与者无法辨别什么是口味, 所以依赖视觉提示吗?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Or does color actually change the experience of taste?
lines.translation: 或者颜色真的会改变品味体验吗?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The key to these questions is the effect of color on expectation.
lines.translation: 这些问题的关键是颜色对期望的影响。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The brain makes predictions using color.
lines.translation: 大脑用颜色做出预测

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: These predictions rely on expectations that come from experience.
lines.translation: 这些预测依赖于经验产生的期望。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Research shows that we're all born liking sweet things and desire to eat them, but we aren't born knowing what the sweet things we crave look like.
lines.translation: 研究表明,我们生来就喜欢甜食 想要吃甜食, 但是我们并不知道我们所渴望的甜食是什么样子。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So we need to learn this over time.
lines.translation: 所以我们需要逐渐了解这一点。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The brain gets information from the environment.
lines.translation: 大脑从环境中获得信息。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And we learn, for example, that fruits go from green and sour to red and ripe and sweet.
lines.translation: 例如,我们学到,水果从绿色和酸味变为红色,成熟和甜美。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Thus, if we see a green berry, we equate its color with a sour taste, and just looking at a red fruit will activate our expectations that it will taste sweet and delicious.
lines.translation: 因此,如果我们看到一个绿色的贝利果, 我们把它的颜色和酸味等同起来, 仅仅看一看红果子, 就会激发我们的期望, 即它将尝到甜甜和美味的味道。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 19. What does the speaker say about our eyes?
lines.translation: 第 19 题：讲话者关于我们的眼睛说了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 20. What does color actually do according to this lecture?
lines.translation: 第 20 题：根据这次讲座,颜色实际上起什么作用?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 21. What does the brain use color to do?
lines.translation: 第 21 题：大脑利用颜色做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Recording 3.
lines.translation: 记录3。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Searching for meaning is something many of us experience throughout our lives.
lines.translation: 寻找意义是我们许多人一生都会经历的事情。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: For some, this meaning is religious, some political and some interpersonal.
lines.translation: 对一些人来说，这种意义是宗教上的；对一些人来说，是政治上的；对另一些人来说，则是人际关系方面的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And having a sense of meaning can bring us happiness.
lines.translation: 而拥有意义感能够带给我们幸福。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: A new study looks at the relationship between meaning and happiness in the context of financial resources.
lines.translation: 一项新的研究从财政资源的角度审视意义与幸福之间的关系。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Rhea Catapano from the University of Toronto and colleagues find meaning is a far weaker predictor of happiness for rich people than poorer people, suggesting economic resources can impact how we experience meaning.
lines.translation: 多伦多大学的Rhea Catapano和同僚发现,对于富人来说,意义远比穷人更弱,意味着经济资源会影响我们如何看待意义。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The team analysed data from over 500,000 people across 123 countries.
lines.translation: 该小组分析了123个国家50多万人的数据。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The first study used data from a daily poll of US residents collected between 2013 and 2015.
lines.translation: 第一份研究使用了2013年至2015年期间收集的美国居民每日民意调查数据。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well-being was tracked using measures of positive affect—whether, during the day before they were surveyed, participants had smiled or laughed a lot or experienced a lot of happiness.
lines.translation: 利用积极影响措施跟踪福利情况,无论是在接受调查的前一天,参与者笑笑或笑得很多,还是经历了许多幸福。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Meaning was measured through a daily "purpose index", which explored the extent to which participants felt that they like what they do every day and are motivated to achieve their goals.
lines.translation: 通过每日的“目的指数”衡量了意义,该指数探讨了参与者在多大程度上认为他们喜欢他们每天做的事情,并愿意实现其目标。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Finally, income levels were assessed.
lines.translation: 最后,对收入水平进行了评估。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The results showed that the correlation between meaning and happiness was strongest among those in lower income brackets.
lines.translation: 结果显示,在低收入阶层中,意义与幸福之间的关系最密切。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But as income levels increased, the correlation became weaker.
lines.translation: 但是,随着收入水平的提高,相互关系变得更弱。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The second study looked at worldwide data.
lines.translation: 第二项研究考察了世界范围的数据。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Happiness was measured using the same questions as in the first study, while meaning was measured using the single question: "Do you feel your life has an important purpose or meaning?" Again, the strength of the relationship between meaning and happiness depended on participants' income: meaning had a greater influence on happiness for those on lower incomes compared to those in higher brackets.
lines.translation: 衡量幸福时使用与第一次研究相同的问题,衡量含义时使用一个单一的问题:“你觉得你的生活有重要的目的或意义吗?” 再说,意义与幸福之间关系的强度取决于参与者的收入:与较高括号中的人相比,意义对低收入者的幸福影响更大。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In the final study, French participants indicated the extent to which they felt they led a purposeful and meaningful life and how much they considered themselves a happy person.
lines.translation: 在最后研究报告中,法国与会者说明了他们觉得自己过着有意义和有意义的生活的程度,以及他们如何认为自己是幸福的人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Finally, rather than using specific income brackets, they placed themselves on a "social ladder", representing where they stand in society with regard to wealth, education, and career.
lines.translation: 最后,他们没有使用具体的收入括号,而是把自己置于“社会阶梯”上,在财富、教育和职业方面代表着他们在社会中所处的位置。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The results from the study duplicated those of the first two.
lines.translation: 研究结果与前两个研究的结果重复。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So overall, meaning and happiness had a stronger relationship in those with fewer resources than those with more.
lines.translation: 总的来说，资源较少的人群中，意义与幸福之间的关系比资源较多的人群更强。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This might be the case because rich individuals have more access to other sources of happiness—many of which will be external, like lack of stress or community.
lines.translation: 这可能是因为富裕人士更容易获得其他幸福来源，其中许多来源是外部的，例如较少的压力或社区支持。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Thus, a focus on an internal sense of satisfaction, purpose or meaning is less important.
lines.translation: 因此，对内在满足感、目标感或意义感的关注就没有那么重要了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 22-25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题22 -25是基于你刚才听到的录音

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 22. What does the speaker say many of us search for throughout our lives?
lines.translation: 第 22 题：说话人说我们许多人终其一生都在寻找什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 23. What do Rhia Catapano and colleagues find about economic resources?
lines.translation: 第 23 题：Rhia Catapano及其同事关于经济资源有什么发现?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 24. What do we learn about Rhia Catapano and colleagues' second study?
lines.translation: 第 24 题：关于Rhia Catapano及其同事的第二项研究,我们了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 25. Why do meaning and happiness have a weaker relationship in those with more resources?
lines.translation: 第 25 题：为什么在拥有更多资源的人群中,意义和幸福之间的关系更弱?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That's the end of listening comprehension.
lines.translation: 听觉理解到此结束
